events.text: The ribbon on {ssp_stake} is tied the way a shopkeeper ties a ribbon, not the way you do. {npc} has lately grown very interested in your work, and asks about it very nicely. {He} has been very nice since that last quarrel. You had not thought much about it until now, standing here with a ribbon.

choices.text: Count everything, twice, and say nothing

effects.log: Everything is there. Everything has also been moved, by someone careful, and put back a finger too far left.

choices.text: Go and find {him}, and talk about that quarrel

effects.log: You start badly. You go on anyway.

choices.text: Hold up the ribbon at dinner

effects.log: You put it down between the dishes and wait.

choices.text: Retie it, and forget about it

effects.log: It is only a ribbon. You tell yourself so for several months.

events.text: A merchant you have never met greets you in the market and knows the name of {ssp_art}. The merchant is embarrassed at once and calls it a lucky guess. That evening {npc} has a new bracelet, and when you ask, {he} says {he} saved for it. {He} has never saved for anything in all the years you have been married, and {he} has never before looked you in the eye while saying so.

choices.text: Find out what the merchant buys

effects.log: All sorts of things, it turns out. There is an account book with very few words in it, and one of them is your name.

choices.text: Ask {him} what {he} is saving up to get away from

effects.log: It comes out sharper than you meant, and then you sit down, and try again.

choices.text: Admire the bracelet

effects.log: {npc} is pleased you noticed. You both go on with the evening.

choices.text: Ask where the money really came from

effects.log: {npc} stops with the cup halfway. You have never seen {him} stop anything halfway.

events.text: The cat that eats what falls from your table has been sick for three days. It is a very old cat, and everyone says so. {npc} says so too. {He} has taken to making your evening soup with {his} own hands, which {he} has not done since the first year, and {he} stays to watch you finish it. You had a quarrel about something. {He} has not mentioned it since. {He} has not mentioned anything.

choices.text: Pour tonight's bowl into the garden and watch the ground

effects.log: Nothing happens to the ground. Nothing has ever been that careful by accident. You begin to keep count of the bowls.

choices.text: Put the bowl down and say what you did wrong

effects.log: It is harder to say than anything you have said to an enemy. You start anyway.

choices.text: Ask {him} to finish the bowl for you

effects.log: {npc} looks at the bowl, and then at you, for slightly too long.

choices.text: Finish the soup. It is good soup

effects.log: It is very good soup. You sleep heavily, and put that down to the winter.

events.text: You wake up tired, these days. The physician says you are working too hard, and takes the fee from {npc}, who has sent for the man twice this year without being asked. They talk at the gate longer than a fee takes. It is the sort of care people remark on. The neighbours think you are very lucky. You think about what you said to {him} last year, in front of everyone.

choices.text: Go to a different physician, three towns away, in a hat

effects.log: The old doctor tastes something on your tongue and asks who cooks for you. You pay double to have the question forgotten.

choices.text: Tell {him} you remember what you said last year

effects.log: {npc} goes very still. You keep going.

choices.text: Ask {him} what the two of them talk about

effects.log: {npc} smiles, and says: you, of course. It is the right answer. It is said a beat late.

choices.text: Rest more, as the physician says

effects.log: You rest. It does not help, and everyone is very kind about it.

events.text: Someone knew you would be on the east road. Three people, in fact, and they were waiting, and it came to nothing, because you were late. You were late because {npc} had asked you to leave at dawn and you overslept. You lie awake with that for a while. You only ever told one person when you leave, and {he} is breathing very evenly beside you, for someone asleep.

choices.text: Tell {him} a different road next time, and watch who waits

effects.log: You say the west road. You take the east one, and pay a boy to sit under a tree on the west one with a basket and a good memory.

choices.text: Wake {him}, and talk about how it has been between you

effects.log: {npc} is awake at once. That tells you something. You talk anyway.

choices.text: Say out loud that someone knew

effects.log: You say it to the ceiling. The breathing beside you does not change at all, and that is the trouble with it.

choices.text: Blame the road, and go to sleep

effects.log: Roads have bad days. You sleep eventually.

events.text: {npc} has a friend you have not met. {ssp_contact}, {he} says, when you ask: nobody, an old acquaintance, you would find it dull. {He} says the name with care, as one sets down something that might chip. Later you learn that this nobody has asked after {ssp_stake}, in passing, at two different dinners. You have been told lately that you do not listen. You begin to listen.

choices.text: Have {ssp_contact} looked into, quietly

effects.log: It costs you a little and teaches you a lot. Nobody who is nobody has this many friends who are afraid of them.

choices.text: Ask what you have stopped listening to

effects.log: {npc} takes so long to answer that you think {he} will not. Then {he} does.

choices.text: Say the name at supper, and ask what they want

effects.log: You say it lightly. {npc} says it back, lightly. Nobody at that table is eating.

choices.text: Let {him} keep {his} friends

effects.log: You are not a jealous person, you tell yourself, and you tell the ceiling, and it is true.

events.text: You named {ssp_other} to the seat beside you at the New Year table, and {npc} moved down one place, smiling, and has gone on smiling ever since. {He} is very gracious to {ssp_other} now. {He} sends over the good tea. {He} has also started keeping accounts, in a hand you do not recognise, of {ssp_stake}. "Someone in this house should," {he} says. "You have so much else to look at."

choices.text: See what is written in those accounts

effects.log: They are excellent accounts. They are also the only full list anywhere of what you own and where you keep it.

choices.text: Go to {his} rooms instead, tonight, and say why you came

effects.log: It has been a long time since you came to that door. You knock, and {he} takes {his} time.

choices.text: Ask who the accounts are for

effects.log: {npc} looks up, still smiling, and asks if you would like to check the sums.

choices.text: Tell yourself the house is calmer than it has been

effects.log: It is calmer. You could hear a pin drop in it.

events.text: A young fighter you beat last spring beat you back this autumn in a practice bout, using the third form of {ssp_art}. It is done badly, the way people do a thing they have learned from a written page. You know of two copies, and one of them is under your own floor. That evening {npc} asks whether anything interesting happened today, and passes the rice.

choices.text: Lift the floorboard after {he} sleeps

effects.log: The dust has been swept back on purpose, with something soft, by someone who knew you would look.

choices.text: Tell {him} you know that something is wrong, and that you helped

effects.log: You say that part first. It is the only part you are sure of.

choices.text: Move on it before the next sale

effects.log: You have seen enough. You will not wait for the third form to walk up to you in a stranger's hands.

choices.text: Put what you know on the table, between the rice and the fish

effects.log: {npc} looks at it. {He} sets down {his} chopsticks and squares them.

choices.text: Say nothing interesting happened

effects.log: {npc} nods, and helps you to more rice.

events.text: The kitchen girl has left in a hurry, and sent word back through an aunt that it would be better not to say why. You find the thing itself behind the flour: a very small jar, sealed, sweet at the rim, with the apothecary's mark scraped off. It could be for rats. There are no rats. {npc} calls from the next room to ask if you are hungry. You stand there longer than a person who is hungry would stand.

choices.text: Take the jar to someone who knows, three towns off

effects.log: The man smells it from across the room and tells you to leave. That means the shop. It also means your house.

choices.text: Bring the jar to {him}, unopened, and say what you did first

effects.log: You set it down between you. You do not ask anything. You begin with the quarrel, and go on from there.

choices.text: Change the jar for one of your own

effects.log: It takes one quiet night. Whatever {npc} does next, {he} will be doing it with what you gave {him}.

choices.text: Carry it into the next room, and put it down in front of {him}

effects.log: {npc} looks up from {his} mending. {He} does not stop mending.

choices.text: Put it back behind the flour

effects.log: It could be for rats. You call back that you are coming.

events.text: The tea you are served at {ssp_contact}'s house is the kind you drink at home. Nobody buys it; {npc} blends it. Your host pours it without a word, watching to see if you notice. It is the most courteous threat anyone has ever made you. Three weeks later {npc} tells you, by the way, that you are looking tired, and might think of handing some of your work to people you trust.

choices.text: Follow the tea: who carries it, and when

effects.log: A girl with a basket, every new moon. You could set a calendar by your own ruin. Now you can read it.

choices.text: Tell {him} you drank the tea, and what you made of the year before it

effects.log: {npc} puts down what {he} is holding. For the first time in years you have all of {his} attention.

choices.text: Move before the next new moon

effects.log: They think you are looking tired. Let them think so for a little longer.

choices.text: Say over dinner that you had some very good tea

effects.log: {npc} goes on serving. {His} hand does not shake at all.

choices.text: Agree that you are tired

effects.log: {npc} is very understanding about it, and lays out your quilt.

events.text: {npc} comes to you late, standing in the door the way {he} did when {he} was small. {ssp_who} has asked {him} to carry a sealed packet across town and tell nobody, and {he} did, and then did it again, and the person at the other end called {him} by the wrong name and laughed. {He} does not know what it means. {He} is only asking whether it means anything. {He} has already worked out that you will say no.

choices.text: Tell {him} the truth, as much as you have

effects.log: {npc} takes it standing. {He} looks older by the end of it than you wanted, and {he} thanks you, which is worse.

choices.text: Ask {him} to carry the next one too, and to look inside

effects.log: {npc} looks at you for a moment and says yes. You have just done to {him} what {ssp_who} did. You both know it.

choices.text: Send {him} away to a relation until the winter

effects.log: {npc} goes, and does not ask why again. It is the kindest thing you can think of, and it does not feel kind.

events.text: {npc} has not spoken a word against {ssp_who} in all the years you have kept this house, and does not begin now. {He} only sets a small account book on the table, open at a page, and leaves {his} finger on one line until you have read it. Then {he} closes it. "I thought you should know where the money goes," {he} says. "I do not want to know why."

choices.text: Thank {him}, and read the rest

effects.log: You read until the lamp gives out. {npc} brings another lamp and goes to bed.

mem.note: took my word, and did not make me say more

choices.text: Ask {him} to tell you all of it

effects.log: {npc} tells you. It costs {him} a good deal. You have not asked what it is like to live beside this, and now you know.

choices.text: Say you did not see anything

effects.log: {npc} looks at you for a while, and takes back the book. {He} does not offer it twice.

mem.note: would not look at what I brought them

events.text: {npc} tells you over the good cups, with enormous pleasure and a very straight face, what {ssp_who} has been doing and with whom. {He} has dates. {He} has clearly had dates for some time, and has been waiting for the moment when it would hurt most, and has picked this one. It is all true. That is the awful thing. You would like very much for it not to be, if only so that {npc} would stop smiling.

choices.text: Thank {him}, and ask for the dates

effects.log: {npc} has written them out. {He} has a very neat hand. You take the paper and do not enjoy it.

choices.text: Ask {him} how long {he} has known

effects.log: A year, {npc} says, and refills your cup. You see it all at once: the two of them, and you in the middle, and nobody in this house looking out for anybody.

mem.note: knows I kept it from them a year

choices.text: Tell {him} to keep it to {him}self

effects.log: {npc} says of course, and goes off, humming. It will be a while before you can drink from that cup.

events.text: {npc} brings it up gently, on a good day. Your heir is young, is {he} not, and has made some choices lately. {He} has heard things. {His} own child would need so little: a word from you, a small change of a name in a book. {He} would never ask, {he} says, asking. There is a folded paper in {his} sleeve already, and {ssp_contact} has been very helpful with the wording.

choices.text: Ask to see the paper

effects.log: {npc} gives it to you at once, with a smile. It has been drafted by someone who knows your house better than you do. Now you know who.

choices.text: Say the name in the book stays where it is

effects.log: {npc} says of course, and thanks you for hearing {him} out, and you can feel the room go cold behind the thanks.

mem.note: would not hear of my child

choices.text: Ask what {he} is really afraid of, for {his} child and for {him}self

effects.log: There is a long silence. The paper stays in the sleeve. You keep asking, and for once you wait for the answer.

events.text: It is over before you hear of it. Everything went, a little at a time, for a year: {ssp_stake}. {ssp_contact} has been buying rounds at the Three Rivers inn. The worst of it is the note, in {npc}'s neat hand, in the empty place: everything you ever taught me, it says, fetched a good price. You came home to it with the mud still on you. {He} is at the table, finishing {his} tea.

choices.text: Sit down across from {him}. Ask what the wedding was worth

effects.log: You talk until morning. It is the most honest night of your marriage. {He} stays, in the end, and you could not say which of you lost.

choices.text: Open the gate and call the neighbours

effects.log: You say it all in the street, plainly, once.

choices.text: Close the door behind you

effects.log: You close it. Nobody in the street hears anything worth repeating, and in the morning you tell them yourself.

choices.text: Walk past {him}, up to bed, and say nothing

effects.log: You do not sleep. Nor does {he}. In the morning neither of you mentions it, and within the month {he} is gone.

events.text: Tonight your hands stop working halfway through the soup. You know what it is at once. It is almost a relief. {npc} is across the table with {his} spoon in the air, looking at you with no expression at all. Your qi does what it was trained to do. It takes all night, and {he} stays for all of it. At dawn you can speak, and you are still alive, and you both know it was not {his} mercy.

choices.text: Ask {him} to bring water

effects.log: {npc} brings it. {His} hands are not steady, and it surprises you both. You drink it. Everything after that is a very long conversation.

choices.text: Say you want {him} out of your house by noon

effects.log: It takes you three tries to say it. {npc} waits politely through all three.

choices.text: Wait until you can stand

effects.log: It is afternoon before you can. {npc} has not run. {He} is at the table when you come down, and {he} looks up.

choices.text: Turn your face to the wall

effects.log: When you can turn back, there is a clean cup beside you, and nobody in the house.

events.text: {ssp_contact} has it all: {ssp_stake}, your hours, your debts, everyone you trust. It went in {npc}'s hand, one new moon at a time. You learn it the morning three people call in three favours you never told anyone you owed. {npc} is doing the household accounts. "I was so tired of being in your way," {he} says, without looking up. "I thought I would see how it is to be in someone else's."

choices.text: Ask {him} what it would take to come back

effects.log: {npc} looks up then. {He} had not considered it. It is a long morning, and neither of you enjoys it, and it is a start.

choices.text: Take the pen out of {his} hand and show {him} the gate

effects.log: You do it in front of the whole household, so nobody has to wonder.

choices.text: Send the household out of the yard

effects.log: They go. Nobody asks. By evening the whole lane has heard, and you do not correct any of it.

choices.text: Say {he} may as well go and see, then

effects.log: {npc} finishes the column first. {He} always was thorough.

events.text: You are sitting in the dark in the storeroom when {npc} comes down at the third hour with a lamp and a copyist's bag. {He} gets all the way to the chest before {he} sees you. Neither of you hurries. {ssp_stake} is under your hand. You have had a year to think about what to say, and it has all gone. {He} is the first to speak. "Well," {he} says, setting down the lamp. "You took your time."

choices.text: Move over, and let {him} sit

effects.log: You sit on the chest together until it gets light. You tell {him} what you did. {He} tells you what {he} did. It comes out about even, and that is the terrible part.

choices.text: Hand {him} the copy you wrote for the occasion

effects.log: You have spent a month getting the errors exactly right. {npc} reads the first page, and starts to laugh, quietly, for the first time in years.

choices.text: Take the bag. Walk {him} to the gate

effects.log: You do not raise your voice. You have been practising.

choices.text: Put out the lamp

effects.log: It does not take long. It takes the rest of your life.

events.text: You have known for months. Tonight, when {npc} sets the bowl in front of you and stays to watch, you pick it up and hold it out across the table, in both hands, as one does for an honoured elder. Nobody says anything. The soup goes cold. A moth gets into it. "How long?" {he} says at last, very evenly. {He} has never been so beautiful to you, or so far away.

choices.text: Pour it on the floor, and say since the quarrel

effects.log: You tell {him} which quarrel. {He} did not know you knew which one. {He} puts {his} head down on the table, and you do not know what to do with your hands.

choices.text: Tell {him} to go on sending the bowl, and to whom to send word

effects.log: {npc} is very quiet. Then {he} asks what you want them to believe. It is the first thing the two of you have planned together in years.

choices.text: Set the bowl down, and say you have packed for {him}

effects.log: There are two bags by the door. You packed them yourself, carefully, with everything that is {his}.

choices.text: Keep holding it out until {he} takes it

effects.log: {npc} looks at you for a long time. Then {he} takes it, and looks at it, and does what {he} always does: finishes what {he} started.

events.text: The girl with the basket has been yours for a year, and you have read every word. Tonight you meet {npc} at the back gate instead, holding the basket. {He} looks at it, and at you. {He} does not ask how long. {He} straightens {his} sleeve, a thing {he} does before guests. "If you have read them," {he} says, "you know I wrote well." You have. It is very good work. You had no idea {he} thought that about you.

choices.text: Say it was all true, the part about you, and go inside together

effects.log: {npc} does not move for a moment. Then {he} comes in, and shuts the gate behind {him}, and neither of you sleeps.

choices.text: Give {him} back the basket, with next month's letter already in it

effects.log: {npc} reads it under the lamp. {He} corrects one word. {ssp_contact} will have a very bad year.

choices.text: Hand {him} the basket, and point down the road

effects.log: {npc} takes it. {He} is halfway down the lane before you can trust your legs.

choices.text: Close the gate behind you both

effects.log: The lane is empty at this hour. It was always a very quiet lane.

events.text: You lay it all out on the long table in front of the household: the ribbon, the merchant's account book, the bracelet, the young fighter and that bad third form. {npc} comes in and sees it, and stops, and then comes and sits in {his} usual place. {He} reads it from one end to the other. "You have got the date wrong on the second one," {he} says. It is the most frightening thing you have ever heard.

choices.text: Send the household out, and ask how it could have gone otherwise

effects.log: They go out. You ask. It takes the rest of the day, and at the end the table is cleared and {he} is still here.

choices.text: Offer {him} a way to keep {his} buyer, on your terms

effects.log: You name what {he} will carry from now on. {npc} thinks about it, with real interest, as a colleague might.

choices.text: Tell {him} the gate is open

effects.log: Nobody in the room breathes. {npc} squares the papers, because they were crooked, and goes.

choices.text: Let the household see this finished

effects.log: You give them a little time to leave the room. Not all of them do.

events.text: You changed the jar. {npc} has been dosing you with sweetened water for a season, and watching you get better, and has started to look puzzled in the mornings. Tonight you cook. You have not cooked in this house for years, and you take a long time over it. You set a bowl in front of {him} and sit down opposite. {He} takes up the spoon out of habit, and smells it, and stops, and looks up.

choices.text: Say it is only soup. Eat from {his} bowl to show {him}

effects.log: You eat. It is not good soup. {npc} starts to shake, and then {he} takes up the spoon and eats the rest, every drop, crying.

choices.text: Say the next one will not be soup, and {he} should go tonight

effects.log: {npc} sets the spoon down very straight. {He} is packed in an hour. {He} leaves the bowl where it is.

choices.text: Say nothing, and wait for {him} to decide

effects.log: It is the longest supper of your life. Whatever is in that bowl, you put it there, and you will say so tomorrow to anyone who asks.

events.text: You go to {ssp_contact} first, in daylight, without an escort. You sit down, pour the tea, and ask what they have been paying for your days. It takes an hour. Then you go home, and {npc} is waiting in the hall. Someone has already run to {him}. {He} has {his} good robe on, and a bag beside {him}, and {he} is not sure which of those {he} will need.

choices.text: Take the bag, and carry it back upstairs

effects.log: {npc} watches you go up with it. {He} stands in the hall for a long time before {he} follows.

choices.text: Tell {him} who pays {him} now

effects.log: {npc} takes that in. Then {he} sits down and asks, in a level voice, what you want them told first.

choices.text: Pick up the bag, and hold it out

effects.log: {npc} takes it. {He} looks about the hall once, at everything {he} kept in order, and goes.

choices.text: Send for no one, and shut the hall doors

effects.log: The servants hear nothing. They stay out of the hall until you call them, and you do not lie to them when you do.

events.text: You put what you have on the table. It is not everything, but it is enough to show you have stopped being stupid. {npc} looks it over and does not bother to deny it. "Do you know what you paid me, all those years?" {he} says, and names a sum, and it is exact. {He} kept accounts. "You taught me {ssp_art} because you could. I got a better price for it than you ever gave me for anything."

choices.text: Ask what would be enough

effects.log: It is a shorter list than you feared, and it is a much harder one. You begin on it that night.

choices.text: Ask what the buyer would pay for a bad copy

effects.log: {npc} blinks, and then something in {his} face wakes up that you have not seen since you first met.

choices.text: Tell {him} to take {his} accounts and go

effects.log: {npc} does. {He} takes the accounts first.

choices.text: Say {he} will not sell anything else

effects.log: You mean it. {npc} sees that you mean it, and does not run. {He} never did run from a thing {he} had priced.

events.text: You put the jar on the table, and {npc} looks at it, and then goes on mending what {he} was mending. "Rats," {he} says. Then, after a few stitches: "Do you remember what you said at my father's funeral, in front of everyone? I do. I have been making you soup ever since." {He} bites off the thread. "It would have taken another two years. I wanted you to have time to notice. You never did notice anything."

choices.text: Say you noticed now, and ask {him} to say the rest

effects.log: {npc} puts the mending down. {He} says the rest. It is a long list, and you are on every line, and you stay until it is done.

choices.text: Say you will have the gate open by morning

effects.log: {npc} nods, and asks if you would like this mended first. You say no. {He} finishes it anyway.

choices.text: Take the mending out of {his} hands

effects.log: {npc} lets you. {He} looks almost relieved. It is the last thing you will ever know about {him}.

events.text: You name {ssp_contact} over dinner, and every new moon for a year, and {npc} goes on serving the fish. "Yes," {he} says. "I wondered when." {He} has thought about this. {He} tells you, in order, each time you looked past {him} in front of someone who mattered, with the place and the year. "They look at me when I speak," {he} says. "Say what you like about them. They do look."

choices.text: Put your chopsticks down, and look at {him}

effects.log: You do. It is a strange thing to do to a person after so many years. {npc} looks back. Neither of you eats. It is a beginning, or something like one.

choices.text: Ask what they would believe, coming from {him}

effects.log: {npc} stops serving. {He} looks at you, properly, and starts to think. You had forgotten how good {he} was at that.

choices.text: Tell {him} to go and be looked at, then

effects.log: {npc} sets down the fish, and takes off {his} apron, and folds it, and goes.

choices.text: Send the servants away from the table

effects.log: They go. The fish goes cold. By morning the whole lane knows what became of it, and you tell them so yourself.

events.text: You have nothing but a feeling, and you say it anyway, and {npc} stares at you. Then {his} eyes fill. All these years, {he} says, and this is what you think. By morning the whole household knows you accused {him} of something, nobody can say what, and they are all being very gentle with {him}. You feel like a fool. You are also, you notice, a little more closely watched.

choices.text: Apologise, in front of them

effects.log: You apologise. {npc} forgives you beautifully, in front of everyone. It takes you some time to understand what that cost you.

mem.note: apologised in front of the whole house, and meant none of it

choices.text: Say nothing, and start looking properly

effects.log: You should have started there. You start there.

events.text: It takes three nights. On the first {npc} lets you talk. On the second {he} tells you what it has been like, and you had no idea, and you say so. On the third {he} goes into the next room and comes back with a small bag. It has a jar in it, or an account book, or a list of names: what it was going to be. "I had not decided," {he} says. "I would like you to know that I had not decided."

choices.text: Burn it together

effects.log: It burns slowly. You both watch it to the end. Nobody says anything clever.

choices.text: Keep it, and say you will never need to open it

effects.log: {npc} looks at you. Then {he} nods, slowly. It goes on a high shelf. It is still there.

events.text: You have only been coming home. The small things have stopped: the very nice voice, the careful questions, whatever it was you half saw. {npc} laughs at supper again, at something you said, and {he} stops, and looks at you for a moment as if {he} has put down something heavy that you never knew about. "What?" you say. "Nothing," {he} says, and helps you to more rice. "Eat."

choices.text: Eat

effects.log: You eat. You will never know how close it was. It is a good supper.

choices.text: Ask {him} what {he} was going to say

effects.log: {npc} thinks about it. "Later," {he} says. "When we are old." {He} is smiling.

events.text: {npc} waited a year to ask, and has clearly been practising. Did {ssp_who} really do what they say? And did it have to go the way it went? {He} is not crying. You would rather {he} were. {He} asks it across the training yard with {his} back very straight, standing exactly the way you stand when someone has hurt you. You had not noticed {he} had learned that.

choices.text: Tell {him} all of it, your part first

effects.log: {npc} listens to the end and nods, and goes back to {his} forms. {He} is not the same with you after that. {He} does trust you, though.

mem.note: told me all of it, even their own part

choices.text: Say {he} will understand when {he} is older

effects.log: {npc} nods politely. It is the politeness {ssp_who} used to use. You feel it go in.

mem.note: would not tell me the truth about my own parent

events.text: You would know that walk anywhere, even across a crowded square. {npc} stops at a sensible distance. {He} has done well. It shows in the shoes. "I heard what they have been saying about you," {he} says. "I did not start most of it. I wanted you to know the difference." You stand there with the whole square going round you. You were married to this person. You can still tell when {he} is lying, and {he} is not.

choices.text: Say it is over, then, and wish {him} well

effects.log: {npc} looks at you a moment longer, and then laughs, the real one, and goes. You find you meant it.

choices.text: Say that next time you will not leave the gate open

effects.log: {npc} bows, exactly as deep as is polite. It is good to know where you stand. Somewhere across the river, your name goes back on a list.

events.text: You are both old enough now to sit in the sun, and out of nothing {npc} says: that was the winter I nearly finished you. {He} tells you the whole of it, then: the day {he} was closest, what stopped {him}, and what it was about, which is not what you thought. {He} is shelling peas the whole time. "I thought you should have it," {he} says. "Before one of us forgets."

choices.text: Take the other half of the peas

effects.log: You shell them together. There is nothing to add. It is the longest you have ever gone without wanting to say anything.

choices.text: Say you always knew

effects.log: You did not. {npc} knows you did not. {He} smiles and lets you have it, which is how you know {he} has forgiven you as well.

choices.text: Go inside

effects.log: You go inside. You do not come out for a while. {He} finishes the peas alone.
